id_and_class.theory_title: Hasker's Unified Experience, Conscious Self, Causal Mind Requires a Brain-Generated Nonphysical Substance
id_and_class.summary: William Hasker argues that a unified conscious experience cannot be spread across the parts of a composite object, so the subject of experience cannot be the brain. Instead the developing brain naturally generates a new, non-composite, nonphysical individual, a ‘field of consciousness’ standing to the brain roughly as a magnetic field stands to a magnet. He calls this emergent dualism: the self depends closely on its brain yet has its own causal powers, including rational inference and libertarian free will.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as an Emergent Self Generated by the Brain

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness belongs to an emergent individual, a unified nonphysical field generated by the brain that is the subject of experience, thought, and choice.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The brain generates and sustains the mind, which is ontologically distinct from it and acts back on it. The mind is tethered to its particular brain, so there is no pairing problem and no need for God to create each soul separately.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence of an individual (what emerges from organized matter is a new substance, over and above new properties)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The emergent self is the single subject to whom all experiences belong. Thoughts lead to other thoughts through their logical relations, which Hasker argues mechanistic physics cannot allow.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal consciousness, including its qualitative character, is irreducible to neural processes and belongs to the emergent self. Hasker’s case rests on unity rather than on qualia or the explanatory gap.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Physical brains; a potentiality for conscious life within matter itself; emergent nonphysical selves with downward causal powers; God, in the theological setting.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Introspective awareness of unified experience, rational inference, and free choice, combined with philosophical argument and neuroscientific findings about mind-brain dependence.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: One non-composite conscious field per brain, integrating all experience into a single phenomenal whole.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal unity; Personal identity; Rational thought; Agency (libertarian free will); Survival
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Emergence of an individual: when biological organization reaches the right level, the brain generates a field of consciousness that is qualitatively unlike its parts and exerts causal influence back on them.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: The self is generated during biological development and is normally sustained by the brain. On Hasker’s own analogy, it would be expected to dissipate when its generator stops.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Spatially generated by and tethered to a particular brain.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The self has genuine downward causal powers: it reasons, acts for purposes, and makes libertarian free choices as an agent cause.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity is primitive to the emergent self. Looking around a room, one has a single visual experience of the whole scene rather than fragments held by separate neurons.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: The potential for consciousness lies in the nature of matter, which keeps emergent dualism continuous with evolutionary biology.
core_claims_and_evidence: A complex state of consciousness cannot exist distributed among the parts of a complex object, so the brain cannot be the subject.
Unified conscious properties need a unified bearer, so what emerges must be an individual.
If mental states act only through their physical properties, rational inference is not what it appears to be.
Libertarian free will requires a unitary agent, which an aggregate of parts is not.
The brain’s constituents are in constant flux, so materialism makes a person a series of distinct individuals.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: arguments from the unity of consciousness, from reason, and from agency, made consistent with neuroscientific evidence of brain dependence.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Rickabaugh argues the unity argument backfires: if a composite brain cannot ground unified consciousness, it is equally unclear how it could generate a simple substance, so emergent dualism faces a combination problem as hard as panpsychism’s. Kim’s critique of emergence implies that downward causal powers violate the causal closure of the physical, and Shrader holds that a key premise about explanatory relations is unmotivated. The magnet analogy breaks down because magnetic fields are not simple and are fully described by the physics of their sources.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: How a distributed brain produces a numerically single nonphysical subject is left unexplained. Interrupted consciousness raises the question whether the field ceases in dreamless sleep or anesthesia and whether the same self returns.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Hasker positions the view between Cartesian dualism, which he says leaves mind-brain correlations arbitrary, and Thomistic dualism, whose Aristotelian metaphysics he rejects. It is more concessive to neuroscience than most substance dualism and more committed than nonreductive physicalism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: The self emerges from the potential of suitably organized matter, but Hasker gives no account of which organizations generate it, so whether an artificial system could is open.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Hasker holds that the self would naturally dissipate when the brain is destroyed, so survival requires God to sustain it directly or provide a resurrection body to generate it.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Hasker offers emergent dualism as the Christian anthropology best fitted to science, allowing for resurrection and a God-given future.

virtual_immortality.rationale: The self is tethered to the particular brain that generates it, and the theory does not say whether a copy would generate the same self or a new one.
